caption:
Is men's skin actually different?
Measurably, yes - which changes the plan more than the menu.

Three things measure differently, and none of them are about grooming. Skin is thicker at several sites. Sebaceous activity generally runs higher. And fine surface lines are fewer, while the ones that do form tend to go deeper.

In 32 healthy volunteers imaged with ultra-high-frequency ultrasound, male skin measured thicker at four of eight body sites - cheek, chest, back and forearm. Thirty-two people at one centre, aged 22 to 74. That is a group average, not a rule about any one face, and thicker is not the same as needing more. It changes where a plan starts, not how much of it you buy.

What it does change: the depth a treatment starts at, the beard line where anything that heats or peels meets hair follicles, and how long visible recovery lasts when less make-up is used to cover it.

Different tissue, same physics. The plan changes, not the principle.

General education only.
